title: Bold access to the throne of grace is incompatible with uncertainty whether God is appeased
source_text: XVI. His adde, quod jubemur adire cum fiducia ad thronum gratiae, Hebr. 4. quodque dicimur in Christo habere fiduciam sive audaciam, & accessum in confidentia per fidem ejus, Ephes. 3. Sed qua cum audacia, qua cum fiducia accedemus ad thronum gratiae, si incertum sit an Deus nobis sit placatus, an infensus? quidve potest aliud in animo gignere talis incertitudo, quam timorem anxium, & meram trepidationem.
pass_a_gloss: Add to these that we are commanded to approach with confidence to the throne of grace (Heb. 4), and that we are said in Christ to have confidence or boldness and access in assurance through faith in him (Eph. 3). But with what boldness, with what confidence shall we approach the throne of grace if it is uncertain whether God is appeased toward us or hostile? And what else can such uncertainty beget in the soul than anxious fear and sheer trembling.
pass_b_english: Scripture bids bold access to grace’s throne.
Uncertainty whether God is for or against us yields only anxious fear, not confidence.
